atoms.text: There are three main states that a volcano can exist in. Active volcanoes are ones that are currently erupting or have erupted recently. An example of an active volcano is Tungurahua in Ecuador.
Dormant volcanoes show no signs of recent eruptions, but they could potentially become active again in the future. Mount Fuji in Japan is an example of a dormant volcano.
An extinct volcano is one that no longer has a magma supply. These volcanoes are predicted to never erupt again. An example of an extinct volcano would be Ben Nevis in Scotland.
